title: Entre la lentitud y el mercado: fricciones en la producción de ciudad pequeña en Colombia
abstract: This article seeks to understand the role of membership in the Cittaslow network in the reconfiguration of territorial production in Pijao and Marulanda, two small Colombian towns that have historically been marginalized. It analyzes, from an ethnographic perspective, the frictions that emerge between aspirations for insertion into global tourist circuits and localized economic practices. It shows that the declaration of “slow town” functions as a symbolic catalyst that activates material transformations and struggles to define what ways of life, what organization and use of space, and what expressions of tradition are legitimate in the present and future of the territory. The tensions surrounding tourism as a “magic solution,” plural economies, and neo-rural projects reveal that Cittaslow does not operate as an external alternative to capitalism, but rather as a field where territorial commodification and practices of reciprocity coexist ambivalently, actively participating in the material and symbolic production of these territories where the rural and the urban converge.

title: Learnable Persistent Wrinkle Formation in Cloth Simulation
abstract: The mechanical memory of fabrics often leads to persistent wrinkles, which reflect key physical properties and habitual wear patterns. Simulating these wrinkles accurately is essential for visual plausibility in digital garments, yet no dedicated approach exists for inferring the parameters that govern their formation due to the lack of precise datasets and estimation methods. We introduce Fabric-101, an inclusive, accurate, and extendable fabric dataset comprising over 101 common fabrics following textile standards. Unlike existing datasets, it captures three physically distinct deformation components (i.e., self-recoverable (elastic), recoverable (friction-driven), and unrecoverable (plastic)), from cyclic loading-unloading measurements. Building on this data, we propose a differentiable cloth simulator combining an elasto-plastic model with friction, designed to capture recoverable and unrecoverable wrinkle formation. Our simulator is differentiable and uses adjoint method to learn fabric physical parameters from the measured hysteresis curves, learning fabric-specific wrinkle behaviors. Through extensive experiments, we demonstrate that our model reproduces persistent wrinkles that are visually and physically similar to real fabrics across diverse materials and motions. Dataset and code are available in https://github.com/GongDeshan/Fabric_101_for_Wrinkles.

title: Ultrastrong bonded metallization on non-weldable thermoset via additive manufacturing
abstract: The continuously increasing flight speed is the relentless pursuit of the high-speed aircraft (HSA). However, the weak bonding between metals and thermosets in HSA antennas, which are susceptible to peeling and detachment, strongly limits their capacity to bear high-speed thermal-vibrational loads. Accordingly, we pose the question that whether a multiscale interfacial interconnection strategy can provide a high-strength manufacturing solution for this hard-to-weld material combination characterized by vast physicochemical disparities. Herein, using a novel solid-state additive manufacturing (AM) strategy termed screw extrusion–plasticizing friction stir deposition (SEFSD) that allows direct metallization on thermosets substrates, we successfully achieved a multiscale-interconnected metallized thermoset comprising macroscale interlocking, microscale anchoring and nanoscale chemical bonding at the Zn/polyimide (PI) interface. We elucidated the friction-stir-driven in-situ formation mechanisms for connections at each scale and demonstrated that the composite load-bearing effect yields a lap-shear strength of (26.73 ± 2.14) MPa, remarkably surpassing the existing methods. Furthermore, the “integrated forming and joining” nature of this solid-state AM strategy highlights its great potential for fabricating robust, conformal hybrid components for advanced antennas and other related applications.

title: Progress and Current Status of Biodegradable Metallic Implants: Mini-Review
abstract: Biodegradable metallic implants have emerged as promising alternatives to conventional permanent implants by eliminating the need for secondary removal surgery while providing temporary mechanical support during tissue healing. This review presents recent advances in biodegradable metallic biomaterials, with particular emphasis on magnesium-, zinc-, and iron-based alloys. The mechanical properties, degradation behaviour, biocompatibility, and clinical potential of these materials are reviewed, highlighting their advantages and current limitations. Recent developments in alloy design, surface engineering, additive manufacturing, nanotechnology, and friction stir processing are discussed as approaches to control degradation while supporting mechanical integrity, osseointegration, and antibacterial performance. The review further examines multifunctional surface coatings and emerging smart implant technologies designed to reduce implant-associated infections and enhance tissue regeneration. The review also distinguishes material-level findings from device-specific clinical evidence across magnesium-, zinc-, and iron-based implants.

title: Preparation and Performance Characterization of Superhydrophobic Ni-Diamond Composite Coatings by Magnetic Field-Assisted Jet Electrodeposition
abstract: The complex and harsh marine environment, combined with the synergistic effect of severe corrosion induced by high salinity and marine biofouling, readily causes corro-sion damage to metallic materials, thereby accelerating their failure process. This study adopted a two-step method via magnetic field‑assisted jet electrodeposition to fabri-cate nickel‑diamond composite coatings. In the first step, a longitudinal dendritic cluster structure was prepared by optimizing the magnetic field intensity and the nickel grain size during jet electrodeposition. Subsequently, the composite coating was obtained by electrodepositing nickel with diamond particles. Finally, superhydropho-bicity was achieved through low‑surface‑energy modification. Experimental results showed that with a nickel particle diameter of 2 μm and a magnetic field intensity of 150 mT, the coating exhibited favorable comprehensive performance, yielding a cluster structure with a water contact angle of 154.9°. The corrosion resistance was character-ized by a self‑corrosion current density of 1.301 × 10⁻⁷ A/cm² and a self‑corrosion po-tential of −0.193 V. Moreover, the incorporation of diamond particles significantly im-proved the wear resistance, as evidenced by a dry friction coefficient as low as 0.145 on the coating surface. title: An Energy-Variational Model for Buried Pipelines under Mining-Induced Ground Movement Considering Pipe Yielding and Pipe-Soil Interface Slip
abstract: In coal-natural gas resource overlap areas, coal seam extraction induces non-uniform ground movements, which in turn cause axial tensile-compressive deformation and potential plastic failure in buried gas pipelines. Existing models based on the linear-elastic pipe assumption are unable to adequately characterize the coupled evolution of pipe-soil interfacial slip, energy transfer, and material yielding. In this study, based on the principle of minimum potential energy, energy-variational governing equations were established by simultaneously considering pipe yielding and interfacial slip states. A nonlinear solution procedure was developed using finite-difference discretization, incremental loading, active-set identification, damped Newton iteration, and Armijo line search, enabling the synchronous updating of pipe yielding states and pipe-soil friction states. Taking a gas pipeline in a coal mining area in Shanxi Province, China, as an engineering case study, the evolution of pipeline displacement, axial stress, and strain energy under different mining stages and limiting frictional resistance conditions was investigated. The results show that increasing the limiting frictional resistance enhances the transfer of mining-induced ground displacement to the pipeline and promotes the axial propagation of the pipe yielding zone. title: IRSC: Intelligent Road Surface Classification Using Computer Vision and Deep Learning
abstract: This study presents an automated method for classifying pavement surface materials using deep learning and computer vision, aiming to improve road maintenance planning and resource allocation. Accurate identification of surface types is crucial in pavement maintenance tasks, as various materials, such as Stone Mastic Asphalt (SMA), High Friction Surfacing (HFS), Hot Rolled Asphalt (HRA), and Surface Dressing (SD), exhibit distinct performance characteristics and maintenance requirements. Traditional manual classification methods are not only time-consuming but also labor-intensive. To address this challenging problem, we propose, develop and evaluate a deep learning-based image classification solution to automate the identification of surface materials. The proposed approach was tested on various road sections across Ireland’s road network to assess its accuracy and generalizability. The current results suggest that combining automated classification with existing manual inspection practices can significantly improve the efficiency and consistency of pavement surface assessments. The proposed approach can facilitate more informed decision-making, optimized resource allocation, and long-term, cost-effective maintenance strategies. Overall, the study highlights the potential of AI-powered tools to streamline visual inspection processes in road asset management.

title: Carbon-based nanomaterials as cutting fluid additives: A review
abstract: Metalworking fluids are commonly used in the machining processes of diverse equipment components to provide cooling, cleaning, rust prevention, and lubrication. The incorporation of cutting fluid additives further enhances their performance. In recent years, carbon-based nanomaterials have attracted attention as environmentally friendly additives for cutting fluids. This work reviews the research progress on carbon-based nanomaterials as cutting fluid additives, analyzes the effects of factors such as the dispersibility of carbon-based nanomaterials, cutting fluid types, and cutting parameters on machining performance, and discusses the friction reduction and anti-wear mechanisms of carbon-based nanomaterials. Finally, current challenges and future prospects for carbon-based cutting fluid additives are outlined. This review aims to provide guidance and references for achieving efficient and environmentally friendly machining of difficult-to-process materials.

title: MEW: An Extensible Multi-user Engaged Workspace for Collaborative 3D Fabrication
abstract: Collaboration in computational fabrication is often hindered by cumbersome 3D asset exchanges and static web viewers. To address this, we propose the Multi-user Engaged Workspace (MEW), an extensible, real-time web system that streamlines 3D asset synchronization and provides seamless access to complex geometry processing. MEW pairs a WebSocket-driven client for synchronized "What You See Is What I See" (WYSIWIS) cross-device viewing with a C++ backend that dynamically loads algorithms as binary plugins. We demonstrate its practical utility via a custom plugin that calculates support material volume for industrial 3D printers, streamlining quotation workflows. Furthermore, by hosting algorithms as executable binaries to eliminate local compilation friction, MEW provides a reliable hub for reproducible research and effortless algorithm evaluation.

title: Epistemic Boundaries of an Empire: The Sa Arrow Poison in Qing China, 1725–1735
journal: East Asian Science Technology and Medicine
abstract: This article examines the Qing empire’s investigation of sa , a poisonous tree sap used by Miao communities in southwest China. Approached as a military crisis rather than a botanical specimen, sa entered the imperial record through urgent attempts to pacify the southwest frontier. Tracing how Qing officials located the tree, verified information through material evidence and animal testing, and attempted to redeploy the poison in campaigns against the Zunghars, this study reveals a mode of frontier knowledge-making grounded in situational, instrumental practice rather than in classical textual traditions. By showing how sa resisted translation into central medical frameworks and could not be reproduced across ecological zones, it also underscores the epistemic boundaries of the eighteenth-century Qing empire and the frictions inherent in early modern knowledge transfer.

title: Experimental Verification of the Effect of Fuel Additives on the Wear of Common Rail Pumps
publisher: Jan Evangelista Purkyně University in Ústí nad Labem
abstract: The article addresses the issue of failures of high-pressure fuel pumps in Common Rail systems and evaluates the influence of fuel additives on their wear. The first part discusses the operating principle of the Common Rail system, the design of high-pressure fuel pumps, and the most common failure modes occurring during their operation. The experimental section focuses on the disassembly and visual analysis of a damaged pump, as well as on the experimental verification of the effects of summer and winter fuel additives in various ratios with diesel fuel. Tribological properties were evaluated using laboratory measurements, supplemented by non-destructive spectral material analysis and hardness testing. The results indicate a significant effect of fuel additives on reducing friction and wear of selected pump components, which may contribute to increased service life and operational reliability.

title: CARGO GRIPLOCK
abstract: In today's global shipping industry, worker safety and cargo security are major concerns, particularly during maritime transportation. Thousands of shipping containers fall overboard annually averaging to 1,382 to 1,500 causing financial losses, environmental pollution, and safety risks. Therefore, innovative solutions are needed to improve container stability and reduce cargo loss at sea.This project aims to introduce GripLock Container Base, an innovative system designed to enhance friction, shock absorption, and container stability during sea transportation. Unlike conventional steel-to-steel contact, GripLock incorporates high-friction composite pads and an enhanced locking mechanism to minimize container sliding and lateral movement.The system consists of a steel base plate attached to the container's corner fitting, reinforced fibre-rubber composite material, a polyurethane layer for grip and shock absorption, and an anti-slip surface texture. Before loading onto a cargo ship, the system would be installed at designated container contact points. Port workers and shipping operators could then follow existing loading procedures while the modified base provides additional grip and stability throughout the voyage.GripLock targets shipping companies, port operators, and container manufacturers. title: Hybrid Computational Mixed Surface Tire Interaction: A Traction Perspective
abstract: This paper examines the tractive performance of a computational radial passenger car tire under winter conditions with salt layered on top of snow. A Continental Cross Contact LX Sport tire, 235/55R19 model, was developed and verified using finite element techniques. This tire model was used in interactions between a rigid road surface and winter contaminants. Salt and snow were modeled as particles using a smoothed particle hydrodynamics technique and calibrated through a simulated direct shear strength test conducted using software called Virtual Performance Solution. The calibrated materials were positioned on a low-coefficient-of-friction road surface with a bilayer snow base topped with a single salt layer. A node-to-segment contact algorithm with edge treatment on a low-friction surface was set up for the tire–road and snow–salt–road contacts. Snow depths of 57, 114, and 170 mm were evaluated, each topped with 25 mm of salt. Angular velocities of 7.542, 37.71, and 75.42 rad/s (equivalent to vehicle speeds of 10, 50, and 100 km/h) and vertical loads of 3.5, 5, and 8 kN were evaluated in all combinations, while maintaining a constant nominal inflation pressure of 228 kPa. This study provides insight into the mechanical influence of granular road salt on tire traction over snow-covered surfaces under varying snow depths, vehicle speeds, and loading conditions, while excluding temperature-dependent melting and freezing-point depression effects.

title: Finite Element Simulation of the Polishing Process for Aluminum Workpieces in the LS-DYNA Software
abstract: Finishing of long cylindrical aluminium components increasingly relies on abrasive belt machining, yet dependable guidelines for selecting its operating regimes remain scarce. To help close this gap, the present work applies explicit dynamic finite element modelling in LS-DYNA to reproduce, at the scale of a single abrasive grain, how the surface of a 6061-T6 alloy is generated during belt polishing. Two idealised grain geometries are contrasted: a truncated cone standing for a fresh abrasive and a half-ellipsoid approximating the same grain after wear. The material response is captured through the Johnson-Cook constitutive and fracture relations together with a Mie-Grüneisen equation of state, so that high strain rates, frictional heating and element erosion are reflected. For each geometry the resultant contact force, the total, sliding and workpiece-side energies, the actual contact area, the contact-zone temperature, the chip morphology and the residual groove profile were examined while the sliding velocity, the indentation depth and the friction coefficient were varied. The computations show that wear-driven rounding of the grain reduces the polishing force at low speeds but simultaneously raises the dissipated energy and the local heating, whereas the conical grain leaves a smoother groove under milder thermal loading. title: Compression Characteristics of Lightweight Foam Soil Based on Silt under Triaxial Stress Conditions
journal: SAE technical papers on CD-ROM/SAE technical paper series
abstract: To explore the compressive and shear characteristics of silt-based foam lightweight soil under triaxial stress conditions, this paper conducts a non-consolidated and non-drained (UU) triaxial test. The effects of different silt dosages (0%, 25%, 50%) and confining pressures (100 kPa, 300 kPa, 500 kPa) on the stress-strain behavior, shear strength and failure mode of materials were systematically studied. The results show that the stress-strain curve of silt-based foamed lightweight soil presents typical strain hardening or softening characteristics, which can be divided into three stages: elastic, hardening/softening and compaction. The increase in confining pressure significantly enhances the peak stress and residual strength, while the increase in silt content leads to a significant decrease in cohesion and internal friction Angle. When the content is 50%, the reduction in cohesion reaches 78.8%. The failure mode transitions from shear failure to compaction failure with the variation of confining pressure and dosage. The shear strength parameter is much higher than the recommended value in the current specification, indicating that the material has good engineering applicability. The research results can provide a theoretical basis for the design and application of light soil based on silt in subgrade engineering.

title: Thermo-mechanical coupling simulation analysis of aramid composites under high-velocity impact
journal: International Conference on New Materials, Machinery, and Vehicle Engineering (NMMVE)
abstract: In order to examine the thermodynamic coupling phenomenon of aramid composite materials during high-speed impact, a coupled dynamic numerical simulation model was developed to model the behavior of bullets piercing through 4 mm thick aramid/epoxy resin layer at velocities of 300300 m/s. The simulations show that because of the low in-plane thermal conductivity of aramid, transient frictional heat cannot spread out, and there is extensive thermal pooling in the region of the perforation. The peak temperature at 900 m/s is instantly 450 K, which is much higher than the glass transition temperature of the epoxy matrix. Such excessive heating causes the matrix to soften very quickly, eliminating the crosswise restriction of the aramid fibers by the matrix, leading to serious micro-buckling and shear cracking. Finally, thermo-mechanical coupling process of degradation caused by thermal pooling, not merely mechanical failure, is the fundamental mechanism of hypervelocity perforation in aramid laminates.

title: The Modelling and Finite Element Analysis of a Tendon-Driven Continuum Robotic Spine for Quadruped Applications
abstract: This ongoing study investigates the modelling and finite element analysis (FEA) of a tendon-driven continuum robotic spine intended for quadruped robots. Existing rigid torsos limit terrain adaptability, while soft or continuum spines are compliant but often suffer from low load-bearing capacity and from models, such as constant curvature, that cannot capture non-uniform deformation under load. This work combines a kinematic description of a three-tendon, disk-segmented spine with a static force-and-moment equilibrium model that includes Coulomb tendon-guide friction, and a nonlinear FEA study of deformation, stress distribution and stiffness under realistic loads. The first stage reproduces a published reference configuration to benchmark the FEA workflow; later stages evaluate candidate materials and design parameters. This version presents the motivation, literature review, mathematical model, FEA methodology and study plan. Results and validation will be added in subsequent versions.

title: Bridging instrumental measurement and sensory perception: Rheo tribological approaches to beverage texture and hydrocolloid functionality
journal: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
abstract: This thesis investigated how rheo-tribological measurements relate to sensory texture perception and formulation stability in dairy and plant-based beverages fortified with functional hydrocolloids. Rheology characterizes viscosity, while tribology evaluates friction and lubrication between moving surfaces; together, these measurements may provide insight into oral processing and ingredient functionality. Two model systems were studied: dairy milk fortified with whey protein microgel as a base for fat-mimetic performance, and oat beverage stabilized with select polysaccharides as plant-based milks which are inherently prone to particle aggregation and phase separation. The overall aim was to determine how ingredient structure, formulation design, and tribological geometry surface influenced lubrication behaviour, and whether these measurements can be used to predict beverage texture and stability. In the dairy system, whey protein microgels with particle sizes of 6 and 20 µm were incorporated into fat-free milk at 15-45% (w/v) and compared with 0% and 2% fat milk controls. Texture was evaluated by a trained sensory panel (n = 13) using intensity ratings for thickness, smoothness, graininess, creaminess, and astringency, together with Check-All-That-Apply profiling. Microgel concentration primarily drove thickness perception through viscosity at oral-relevant shear rates, while particle size significantly influenced smoothness, graininess, and overall fat-mimetic performance.

title: Evaluation of the Effect of Die Surface Condition on Non-Steady-State Deformation and Force Behavior in Pure Copper Micro-Extrusion Using Geometrically Necessary Dislocation Density
abstract: In recent years, copper-based conductive and thermal management components have required fine structures for miniaturization and enhanced functionality. Micro-forming is an excellent processing method characterized by high productivity and suitability for mass production. Since micro-forming is highly influenced by tribological conditions, proper setting of die surface conditions is essential. In micro-extrusion, surface coatings such as diamond-like carbon (DLC) have been explored to optimize tribological conditions. However, the effects of die surface properties on the internal deformation state (evolution of the work-hardened microstructure and the resulting plastic-flow) during forming have not been quantitatively characterized. In this study, micro-extrusion tests of pure copper were conducted using two types of dies: one with a DLC coating and one without any coating. Changes in the internal deformation with stroke progression were analyzed using kernel average misorientation (KAM) maps and geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density. Measurement of GND density enabled quantitative evaluation of the internal deformation state within the material. Consequently, changes in GND density with stroke progression closely corresponded to the force behavior, suggesting that die surface conditions significantly affect not only the frictional state at the material surface but also the internal deformation.

title: Pectus implant stainless-steel abrasion in the pleural cavity induces systemic metal contamination in mice
abstract: Introduction: Patients undergoing minimally-invasive repair of pectus excavatum (MIRPE) typically receive stainless-steel bars and stabilizers as separate implants, that allow small metal-to-metal movements while breathing. In a previous clinical study, we have detected elevated chromium and nickel levels in blood and urine of these patients. To test the hypothesis that metal-to-metal friction is the key factor for metal contamination following MIRPE, we developed a mouse model to examine the effect of metal implants and abrasion in the pleural cavity. Material & Methods: The study was approved by the Institutional Animal Care Committee (33.12-42502-04-16/2201). Mice were hold in metal-free cages and fed control diet C1000. Five experimental groups were established: group A received stainless-steel particles intrapleurally, imitating metal-to-metal abrasion, group B received small stainless-steel pieces intrapleurally, group C received small stainless-steel pieces subcutaneously, group D received small titanium-coated pieces intrapleurally and the control group received alginate intrapleurally. title: Strength characteristics of clayey CH4 and CO2 hydrate-bearing sediments considering temperature-pressure conditions
abstract: The shear strength of clayey hydrate-bearing sediments (HBSs) is jointly controlled by hydrate saturation and temperature-pressure conditions, yet most existing strength criteria do not explicitly incorporate the thermodynamic state of hydrate. This study develops a temperature-pressure-dependent strength framework for clayey methane hydrate-bearing sediment (MHBS) and carbon dioxide hydrate-bearing sediment (CDHBS) using the discrete element method (DEM). The temperature-pressure parameter L incorporated with phase equilibrium boundary is introduced to link temperature and pore pressure to hydrate-bond stiffness and strength. Subsequently, conventional triaxial compression simulations are conducted for clayey MHBS and CDHBS containing pure CH 4 hydrate and pure CO 2 hydrate, under the same clay-skeleton representation and loading procedure. The DEM simulations account for hydrate cementation, thermal-hydro-mechanical-chemical (THMC) coupling and aggregate crushing. Meanwhile, these simulations also capture the effects of hydrate type, hydrate saturation, and confinement on bond degradation, contact-network evolution, and macroscopic strength. The results show that hydrate-bond degradation progressively transfers load from cementation to particle contacts, while aggregate crushing further modifies the contact network. title: Tough, Hysteresis-Free Hydrogels via Adaptive Single-Molecule Knots
abstract: The intrinsic stochasticity of conventional polymer networks can generate heterogeneous stress distributions that limit mechanical performance and contribute to the persistent trade-off between toughness and reversibility. Here, we address this limitation through a paradigm of entanglement-statistics engineering. We incorporate single-chain nanoparticles (SCNPs) featuring intramolecular loops as topological anchors. Through in situ polymerization, growing network chains can penetrate these loops, integrating the SCNPs into an architecture of adaptive single-molecule knots. Within this redistributed topological landscape, hydration-dependent knot conformation regulates the mechanical response. Crucially, compact knots in the as-prepared state function as reservoirs of “hidden length” that can be progressively recruited during deformation, enabling extreme extensibility (>2600%), whereas solvated knots in the swollen state facilitate reversible frictional sliding and ultralow hysteresis. This adaptive strategy enables hydrogels to combine high toughness, extreme extensibility, and excellent recoverability, establishing active topology design as a route toward mechanically adaptive soft materials.

title: When AI Helps Organize Our Thoughts: Neurodiversity and Academic Workflows in Higher Education
abstract: Presented to a live audience at the 2026 EDUCAUSE Annual Conference in Denver, Colorado, this presentation explores how generative artificial intelligence can serve as cognitive scaffolding for neurodivergent professionals and support more inclusive academic workflows. Drawing on cognitive load theory, the extended mind, and cognitive offloading, it examines opportunities to reduce barriers related to organizing information, initiating tasks, planning, and professional communication. Examples from research, teaching, library systems, metadata, and administration illustrate how AI can help structure complex inputs while preserving human judgment, agency, and individual voice. The presentation offers a practical framework for identifying cognitive friction and designing workflows that accommodate diverse ways of thinking, creating more space for substantive intellectual and creative work.AI Use Disclosure: ChatGPT (OpenAI) assisted with idea organization, wording, slide development, and descriptive metadata; Nano Banana in Google Gemini generated images. title: Simulation and Experimental Investigation of Rapid Fused Deposition Modeling for Resin‐Bonded Diamond Grinding Wheels
abstract: This study presents a fused deposition modeling‐based method for fabricating resin‐bonded diamond grinding wheels to address limitations of conventional microwheel manufacturing, including low material utilization, high equipment cost, and demanding mold precision. Molecular dynamics simulations and finite element analysis were combined to investigate the rheological behavior of acrylonitrile butadiene styrene (ABS)/polyvinyl chloride (PVC)/diamond abrasive /dioctyl phthalate (DOP) composites and optimize five resin‐bonded diamond composite (RDC) formulations (RDC1–RDC5). A thermo‐mechanical model of the nozzle flow channel and grinding wheel was established in Ansys Workbench to analyze temperature, viscosity, velocity, stress, and strain distributions. Results show that DOP improves melt flowability by reducing polymer‐chain entanglement and interfacial friction. Experimental validation demonstrates that a 0.1 mm layer thickness and 30 mm/s printing speed effectively reduce thermal stress and strain, while a 1.25 mm wall thickness promotes structural densification. Surface morphology confirms that 0.1 mm layers are free of visible microdefects, whereas larger layer thicknesses (0.15–0.2 mm) produce interlayer defects. These findings provide optimized processing parameters and a theoretical basis for high‐precision, low‐cost additive manufacturing of micro diamond grinding wheels for hard and brittle material machining.

title: Investigation of Intensive Wear Zones of an Oil Press Screw During Oilseed Processing
abstract: The article presents a computational and experimental study of the wear of an oil press screw during the processing of oilseed raw materials. The study aimed to determine the most heavily loaded zones of the screw by comparing an engineering calculation model with experimental data. The calculation model included a linear pressure distribution along the screw, Coulomb’s law to estimate friction, and Archard’s equation to predict linear wear. Experimental verification was conducted by measuring changes in the geometric parameters of the screw flights across three screw zones after operation. The calculated annual wear in zones I, II, and III was 0.166, 0.243, and 0.318 mm/year, respectively, while the experimental values were 0.178, 0.260, and 0.348 mm/year, respectively. The deviation between the calculated and experimental data was within 7.2-9.4%, which confirms the applicability of the proposed model for preliminary wear assessment. It was established that the maximum wear is localized in zone III, corresponding to the final compression and material discharge section. The obtained results justify the need for local strengthening or the application of a wear-resistant coating to the most heavily loaded screw sections. title: Geotechnical Improvement of Soil with Glass, Marble, Ceramic, Plastic, and Concrete Wastes: A Review of Performance and Mechanisms
abstract: The demand for sustainable construction practices has increased the focus on recycling and reusing industrial and construction waste in geotechnical engineering. This review investigates the use of glass waste (GW), marble dust (MD), ceramic waste (CW), plastic waste (PW), and concrete waste (CoW) to improve soil geotechnical properties. In one of the reviewed studies, adding 27% glass powder (GP) to high-plasticity clay increased the unconfined compressive strength (qu) by 98.58%, whereas other studies reported favorable performance at lower GP contents, depending on the soil type and the investigated property. Glass waste additions of up to 20% were also reported to improve California bearing ratio (CBR) values in the reviewed studies. For marble dust (MD), a 10% addition doubled the qu value of low-plasticity silty clay in one study, while other investigations reported improvements at different dosages. These findings indicate that the effectiveness and optimum content of each waste material depend on the soil characteristics and the geotechnical property being evaluated. Introducing coarse CoW particles raised the maximum dry density γmax values, whereas mixing them with fine CoW particles decreased them. title: Miniature Tensile-Shear Testing of Local Shear Bonding Strength in AFSD Al6061 Cladding
abstract: Cladding and repair processes require strong bonding between the deposited material and the original substrate. Additive Friction Stir Deposition (AFSD) is a promising solid-state process for these applications, but the local bonding strength of AFSD-deposited Al6061 has not been thoroughly examined. Thin cladding layers are difficult to evaluate using conventional large tensile-shear specimens. In this study, a miniature tensile shear specimen was designed to measure local shear strength within a thin AFSD Al6061 cladding layer. The shear strength was measured at the substrate/deposit interface and at 0.5 mm above the interface within the deposited layer. Finite element analysis was used to evaluate the stress distribution in the specimen. The results showed that the selected specimen geometry concentrated stress in the target region, supporting its use for localized shear-strength measurement. The average shear strength was about 159 MPa at the substrate/deposit interface and 139 MPa at 0.5 mm above the interface within the layer. The interface strength was about 79% of the shear strength of bulk Al6061-T6, showing strong bonding between the deposited material and the substrate. The results also showed that the interface was stronger than the cladding material tested 0.5 mm above it. EBSD analysis showed substantial grain refinement after AFSD. title: Layer thickness effects on FDM elastomer tribology: a systematic review
journal: Journal of Achievements of Materials and Manufacturing Engineering
abstract: The systematic review investigates the influence of FDM/FFF process parameters, particularly layer thickness, on the tribological performance of elastomeric and flexible polymer components, focusing on mechanisms through which printed architecture influences friction and wear. Peer-reviewed studies were identified from Scopus, Web of Science and SpringerLink and ScienceDirect. Following deduplication, 665 records were screened; 155 full-text records were then assessed, yielding 103 included studies. Data were categorised as direct core, indirect tribology, mechanistic or comparator evidence. Structured quantitative comparisons and a narrative mechanistic synthesis were undertaken; conventional meta-analysis was not performed due to substantial heterogeneity and limited direct evidence. One included study simultaneously investigated FDM-printed TPU, variation in layer thickness and tribological outcomes. Overall, the evidence indicates that layer thickness can affect surface roughness, porosity, interlayer structure and the mechanical response of polymers to shear, but the direction and magnitude of this tribological effect is not consistent across printed materials. The complete causal process-structure-tribology relationship has seldom been measured under the same experiment. The evidence base is heterogeneous in terms of materials, process conditions, tribological protocols and outcome definitions. title: Data and Code for: Procyclical Fiscal Policy and Asset Market Incompleteness
publisher: Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research
abstract: We develop a model of the joint behavior of optimal tax rates and government spending over the business cycle to explain procyclical fiscal policy in emerging markets. Our setup relies on financial frictions, which have been shown to be critical features of emerging markets, captured by various degrees of asset market incompleteness as well as varying levels of debt-elastic interest rate spreads. We show that incomplete markets can account for procyclical government spending but not necessarily procyclical tax policy. Explaining procyclical tax policy also requires that the ratio of private to public consumption comoves positively with the business cycle. This replication package provides the code, data, and supporting materials for the figures and tables of the article: MATLAB programs for the DSGE and two-period models, Stata and R programs for the empirical exercises, the redistributable data, a codebook (AEJM_Codebook.xlsx), LICENSE.txt and a README (Markdown and PDF). Restricted data (an internal IMF World Economic Outlook vintage and J.P. Morgan EMBIG sovereign spreads) are not included; the README documents their access conditions and preservation.

title: Decision-driven design and verification of a heavy-duty transfer chassis for manufacturing intralogistics
journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part B Journal of Engineering Manufacture
abstract: This study presents the design and architecture-level verification of a heavy-duty transfer chassis for manufacturing intralogistics, formulated as a decision-driven engineering problem rather than a numerical optimization task. The system integrates modular subframes, mechanically synchronized steering, bidirectional towing, and geometrically referenced clamping to address maneuverability, adaptability, and global structural-performance requirements under industrial constraints. Finite element analysis was employed as a decision-support tool to assess global static stress, deformation, and stiffness responses under representative loading scenarios. The static assessment was supplemented by a preliminary parent-material fatigue evaluation based on the Marin methodology and the Goodman criterion. Within the adopted loading, material, contact, and boundary-condition assumptions, the evaluated results supported the selection of the proposed architecture for the defined decision horizon. The final configuration achieved an 18% mass reduction while maintaining the evaluated global stiffness and static-response requirements. Full-scale displacement measurements showed deviations of approximately 3.1%–5.3% from the numerical predictions, supporting the consistency of the predicted global structural response. title: FIBRILLATED PTFE FOR DURABLE TRANSFER FILM FORMATION IN SOLID LUBRICANT POLYMER COMPOSITES
journal: Library, Museums and Press - UDSpace (University of Delaware)
abstract: Polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) is widely used as a solid lubricant because of its low friction, chemical inertness, and thermal stability, but its high wear limits durable sliding applications. Low wear requires transferred PTFE to remain at the counterface long enough to form a protective transfer film. The ultra-low-wear PTFE composite literature explains durable lubrication through two established mechanisms: bulk reinforcement, which arrests subsurface cracking and reduces debris size, and tribochemistry, which strengthens transferred material once it has accumulated at the interface. However, these two mechanisms cannot explain two key observations. Heat treatment can eliminate ultra-low wear in alumina/PTFE composites even when the alumina filler system is preserved, and prior studies have shown that a fibrillation-capable PTFE structural state can reduce wear without any filler at all. Both results point to PTFE morphology as an active contributor to durable lubrication that reinforcement and tribochemistry alone cannot account for. This dissertation tests the hypothesis that shear-activated PTFE fibrillation provides a third, mechanically distinct mechanism, a mechanical retention step that helps debris adhere to the counterface, nucleate the transfer film, and remain engaged long enough for reinforcement and tribochemistry to take effect. title: Comparison of Experimental and Computational Models for Lunar Anchors with Compliant Mechanisms
abstract: Deployable and compliant mechanisms are useful for the development of shape-changing, foldable, compact, and material-efficient spatial structures. Geosystems for lunar infrastructure must resist uplift forces while remaining compact for efficient transport and material use—a requirement that conventional rigid pile systems are not designed to meet. Deployable panel structures employ compliant thin-wall attachments, referred to as awns, to a central shaft to increase functional surface area through passive geometric transformation during torque-driven actuation. This increased surface area correlates to higher skin friction to better resist axial tensile forces. The structural behavior of these foldable panel attachments and their interaction with the surrounding medium during large-deformation deployment are explored using both small-scale experimental testing and computational methods involving dynamic relaxation (DR). title: China’s Dual-Flank Strategy in South Asia: Assessing the Geopolitical Implications of the Pakistan-Bangladesh Axes on India’s Security Architecture
abstract: The post-colonial geopolitical equilibrium of South Asia, long sustained by traditional Westphalian sovereignty and fragmented, localized threat perceptions, is undergoing a profound structural reconfiguration. This chapter argues that the classic bilateral paradigms traditionally used to evaluate regional friction are no longer sufficient. Instead, it introduces a comprehensive, system-level analysis anchored in John Mearsheimer’s paradigm of Offensive Realism and Nicholas Spykman’s spatial mechanics of the Rimland. The central thesis posits that the People’s Republic of China (PRC) has transitioned away from a purely localized border containment strategy along the Himalayas. Instead, Beijing is actively operationalizing a highly synchronized, multi-vectored structural encirclement mechanism termed the "Elastic Pincer Framework." By cultivating, financing, and integrating asymmetric strategic anchors on India’s immediate periphery—specifically through Pakistan on the Western Flank and a transitioning Bangladesh on the Eastern Flank—China seeks to freeze India's geopolitical rise. This systematic encirclement forces New Delhi to exhaust its finite material, fiscal, and diplomatic capital on localized survival, effectively neutralizing its potential to project power as a peer competitor in the wider Indo-Pacific theater.

title: Cross-Linking Architecture Governs Interactions between Opposing Microgel Monolayers Probed by Total Internal Reflection Microscopy
abstract: We investigate how internal network architecture governs interlayer interactions and confined dynamics in microgel monolayers using total internal reflection microscopy (TIRM). Three poly(N-isopropylacrylamide) (PNIPAM) microgels with distinct architectures─dense-core (DC), dense-shell (DS), and homogeneous (HOMO)─were assembled into opposing monolayers on colloidal probes and planar substrates. Analysis of equilibrium height distributions, interaction potentials, and effective elastic parameters reveals pronounced architecture-dependent responses to salt-induced charge screening. DC microgels exhibit strong salt sensitivity and a transition from recovery-dominated to compression-dominated elasticity, whereas the dense shell of DS microgels suppresses deformation and renders interlayer mechanics largely insensitive to ionic strength. HOMO microgels primarily display salt-enhanced compression due to their uniform network structure. Confined diffusion analysis further shows nonlinear, asymmetric compression–recovery behavior and architecture-dependent subdiffusive dynamics, with vertical motion strongly regulated by interlayer confinement and lateral motion governed by local frictional environments. These results establish a microscopic link among microgel architecture, interlayer elasticity, and near-wall hydrodynamics, providing mechanistic insight into the collective mechanical behavior and interfacial dynamics of microgel-based soft materials.

title: Detection and Slipperiness Estimation of Road Using Multi-Sensor and Vision Data in Arctic Conditions
abstract: Autonomous vehicles operating in Arctic regions could face challenges due to snow and ice-covered roads, low vision, and rapidly changing weather conditions, all of which negatively impact sensor reliability and decision-making. In autonomous driving, safe navigation plays a significant role, which could be achieved with reliable detection of drivable paths and evaluation of road slipperiness. However, the current studies lack a multi-sensor dataset that includes a wide range of driving scenarios in Arctic regions in varying environmental conditions. To address these challenges, this thesis proposes a solution for collection, integration, and analysis of multi-sensor data obtained in Arctic driving environments. This thesis has improved perception and environmental awareness in Arctic driving environments by combining multi-sensor data. The challenges of autonomous driving in Arctic environments have addressed in this thesis by developing a methodology for collection, integration, and analysis of multi-sensor data. The multi sensor data was collected from Arctic road-driving environments using sensors including LiDAR, environmental, friction, and camera sensors. This multimodal sensor data provides a way to improve perception and environmental awareness of autonomous driving in Arctic environments. title: Deep-Learning-Enhanced Coupled Flow-Geomechanical Upscaling Technique for Heterogeneous Soil and Rock Mass
journal: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
abstract: The geomechanical behaviour of heterogeneous soils is strongly influenced by material contrast, spatial variability, and coupled deformation–fluid flow processes. Although high-resolution coupled flow–geomechanical simulations can capture these responses, their computational cost becomes prohibitive for realistic three-dimensional models. This thesis develops a deep-learning-assisted upscaling framework to efficiently predict anisotropic geomechanical properties from grid-based heterogeneous soil realizations. Oil sands with interbedded sand and shale are used as a representative example due to their strong material contrast and directional heterogeneity. A three-dimensional convolutional neural network (3D CNN) was developed and trained using datasets generated from fine-scale numerical triaxial compression simulations conducted under multiple loading directions and drainage conditions. The trained 3D CNN model predicts complete stress–strain response curves, from which key geomechanical parameters, including stiffness, peak shear strength, friction angle, dilation angle, and pore pressure evolution, are derived. title: Multifunctional performance of ceramic reinforced magnesium metal matrix composites through microstructural engineering and thermal analysis
journal: The Journal of Strain Analysis for Engineering Design
abstract: This research analysis the effect of zirconium nitride (ZrN) reinforcement on the mechanical, tribological, microstructural, and thermophysical characteristics of the AZ80 magnesium alloy-based metal matrix composite. The composites made with 0, 3, 6, and 9 wt.% ZrN were analyzed by scanning electron microscopy (SEM), energy-dispersive spectroscopy, mechanical testing, dry sliding wear testing, and laser flash analysis (LFA). The hardness, flexural strength, tensile strength, yield strength of the composites progressively increased with increasing ZrN content, whereas elongation decreased. The hardness and ultimate tensile strength values at 9 wt. % ZrN were 110 ± 4 VHN and 305 ± 8 MPa, respectively, which are higher than those obtained for the unreinforced alloy (68 ± 2 VHN and 210 ± 5 MPa). The wear rate and coefficient of friction were also significantly reduced to 2.1 × 10 −6 mm 3 /N·m and 0.31, respectively, at a load of 10 N. Microstructure analysis showed that with the increase in ZrN content, there was an improvement in the distribution of the reinforcements and the interaction between the matrix and the particles. The proposed model has a lower error rate, with an Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.02, an Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.04, and an Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 0.08. The results show that AZ80 composites reinforced with ZrN are promising materials for lightweight structural applications where improved strength and wear resistance are required.

title: A Novel Fe-M(Nb,Mo,Cr)-C-B Coating on AISI 4140 Steel: Microstructural, Indentation and Wear Characterization
abstract: Fe-based coatings containing hard secondary phases are a cost-effective alternative to Co- and Ni-based hardfacings for improving the wear resistance of steel components. A gas-atomized Fe-M(Nb,Mo,Cr)-C-B alloy was consolidated onto AISI 4140 steel by hot pressing at 1050 °C for 30 min under 50 MPa, producing a coating approximately 1 mm thick. X-ray diffraction of the powder and the consolidated coating identified an α-Fe matrix with M7(C,B)3 and M(C,B) secondary phases. The coating-substrate interface was continuous, with a narrow interdiffusion zone. Statistical nanoindentation gave 14.2 ± 4.4 GPa for the coating and 10.5 ± 1.3 GPa for the substrate. Under dry-sliding conditions, the coating exhibited a specific wear rate of (1.5 ± 0.4) × 10−6 mm3 N−1 m−1, approximately 26 times lower than that of AISI 4140 ((3.9 ± 1.9) × 10−5 mm3 N−1 m−1, 20 N, three tests per material), and a lower mean coefficient of friction (0.45 ± 0.06 vs. 0.54 ± 0.10). Worn-surface analysis indicated mild oxidative and micro-abrasive wear of the coating, in contrast to the adhesive-abrasive wear of the substrate. These results make the alloy a promising feedstock for wear-resistant powder-based coatings.

title: Jammed Nano-Silica/Cross-Linked Polyether Composite Breaks the Strength–Toughness Trade-Off in Polyamide 6
abstract: The strength-toughness trade-off in polyamide 6 (PA6) persists because most existing toughening strategies require high additive loadings, which inevitably sacrifice tensile properties. Herein, we report an in situ constructed nano-silica@cross-linked polyether (CPE) nanocomposite that serves as an exceptionally effective, low-dose toughening phase. This highly filled system features densely packed hydrophilic nano-silica within the CPE domains. The epoxy cross-linker covalently bonds with the terminal amine groups of PA6, ensuring spontaneous interfacial compatibilization between the toughening domains and the matrix. Impact energy is primarily dissipated through intense interparticle friction and collisions among the jammed nanoparticles confined within the toughening domains, a mechanism resembling shear-thickening fluids. With a total additive content of only 5 wt %, this nanocomposite toughening phase transforms PA6 into a supertough material without sacrificing tensile strength. The optimal formulation (2.0%nano-silica@3.0%CPE/PA6) delivers a notched Charpy impact strength of 125.85 kJ/m2 at 23 °C and 109.75 kJ/m2 at −30 °C, corresponding to 14.7-fold and 20.6-fold improvements over neat PA6, respectively, while retaining a tensile strength of 59.6 MPa, which is comparable to that of neat PA6 (58.3 MPa). This work presents a highly efficient strategy for toughening engineering plastics.

title: Computational study of Fe 3 O 4 nanofluid and geometry effects in double-pipe heat exchangers
abstract: Introduction: The performance of Fe 3 O 4 nanofluid in concentric pipe heat exchangers was evaluated against pure water and ethylene glycol as baselines to determine thermal–hydraulic feasibility. Materials and methods: This was achieved by computationally modelling heat transfer across straight, 90° T-shaped and 45° Y-shaped double-pipe geometries and two single-bend controls (a 90° elbow and a 45° bend), with water or ethylene glycol in the inner tube. Results: The nanofluid raised the annulus-side convective heat transfer coefficient by a factor of 1.114–1.126 in every geometry and leg ( h ∝ k 0.53 for a 23% rise in conductivity), with no change in friction factor or pressure drop. Because the annular film carries 38–52% of the thermal resistance with water in the inner tube and about 7% with ethylene glycol, the overall coefficient rose by 4.2–6.0% and 0.7–1.4%, respectively. Junctions and bends raised the local wall heat flux by 10–31% within about 0.2 m of the junction but contributed at most 2% of the heat duty; downstream legs recovered the straight-pipe coefficient within 1.3%, and the junctions added loss coefficients of 0.2–1.4. Conclusions: An ultra-dilute Fe 3 O 4 suspension gives a modest, penalty-free gain that scales with the share of thermal resistance on the side where it is used, whereas junctions and bends act only locally and at a pressure cost; the two effects are independent and additive.

title: Peer Review Report For: From Curing to Caring: Bridging the Leadership and Soft-Skills Gap in Moroccan Medical Education [version 1; peer review: 1 not approved]
abstract: Background Medical leadership and soft skills are critical for effective healthcare; those competencies are crucial for day-to-day medical practice, particularly in low to middle-income countries like Morocco, where leading teams and managing patients present greater challenges due to human and material resource constraints. Yet Moroccan medical training remains disproportionately focused on technical competencies. This study assessed the professional experience of 32 interns in a low- to middle-income developing nation to investigate the alignment between their learning priorities and professional realities. Methods A cross-sectional survey was conducted involving the full cohort of interns at Tangier University Hospital. We assessed learning priorities, daily work time allocation, conflict management history, and communication quality using an anonymous questionnaire. Results While interns ranked conflict management as their lowest learning priority, they spent 23% of their daily time dealing with conflicts and 47.3% on administrative tasks. Furthermore, communication with colleagues was rated poorly (4/10), and 36% of interns expressed dissatisfaction with existing conflict resolution processes. Conclusion Our findings highlight a fundamental gap and a paradox between the skills interns value and the competencies actually required in their high-stress work environments. title: Interfacial thermal response and bonding behavior of CF/PEEK composites joined by tangential ultrasonic welding without energy directors
abstract: Tangential ultrasonic welding without energy directors places carbon fiber-reinforced polyether ether ketone (CF/PEEK) laminates in direct contact. The spatial distribution of interfacial bonding provides a basis for understanding joint load-bearing performance. This study combines an interfacial frictional heating model, lap shear testing, industrial computed tomography (CT) of representative joints, and fracture-surface observations. Thermal responses and bonding characteristics are compared across welding force, amplitude, and time series. The calculations locate high-temperature regions mainly at the overlap edges and predict higher edge temperature peaks with increasing amplitude. At 150 N and a single-sided amplitude of 12 µm, the 800 ms joint reached the highest measured apparent lap shear strength, 9.84 MPa. Its effective fracture-surface area fraction was 46.0%. The corresponding values for the 1000 ms joint were 5.73 MPa and 32.9%, accompanied by local gaps and resin extrusion. Effective fracture-surface area fractions and strengths changed in the same direction in the amplitude and time series. The force series exhibited a different area–strength relationship. CT and microscopic fracture-surface observations linked these differences to interfacial continuity, local pores, and material damage. The results support assessing joints without energy directors through both effective fracture-surface coverage and local bonding conditions.

title: The pedagogy of “smart intervention”: aligning socio-spatial justice and circularity in the adaptive re-programming of Alexandria's Cotton Bourse
abstract: Purpose Driven by the climate crisis and systemic urban precarity in the Global South, this article evaluates a novel pedagogical framework for interior architecture education. It explores how the “Smart Intervention” pedagogical framework combining material circularity with socio-spatial justice trains students to transform dormant, post-industrial heritage sites like Alexandria's Cotton Bourse into socially responsive community assets, moving beyond the limitations of static historicist preservation. Design/methodology/approach This research employs a qualitative Research-by-Design (RbD) methodology embedded within a 15-week interior architecture bachelor design studio. Using Alexandria's Cotton Bourse in Mena El-Basal as an empirical living laboratory, the methodology integrates archival analysis, physical structural audits, qualitative community ethnography (N = 45), iterative design prototyping and a qualitative expert appraisal (N = 3 jurors). The “Smart Intervention” framework operationalizes Open Building principles (Support vs. Infill) across a purposive sample of three student project typologies. Findings The study illustrates how applying the “Smart Intervention” pedagogical framework equips future interior architects to move past purely aesthetic adaptive reuse. The resulting speculative spatial proposals illustrate how circular material flows such as dry-joint timber and steel friction clamps, structural reversibility and socio-spatial programming can coexist. abstract: Medical–rehabilitation–education (MRE) integration connects three service systems during early childhood, and in doing so it moves the family from the receiving end of services to the delivering end of intervention. Policy documents and evidence-based research alike acknowledge this shift, yet the operational target of empowerment remains, for the most part, the skills of an individual caregiver. The arrangement rests on a premise that is rarely stated: that the family is a family unit of stable structure whose caregiving resources can be coordinated. Taking as its observation point families that are divorced, separated, single-parent, reconstituted, grandparent-led, or locked in prolonged high discord, this paper combines conceptual analysis with policy text analysis, supplemented by publicly available material on local practice in Zhejiang Province, to ask where that premise fails. Three failure mechanisms are identified: implementation fidelity decays as relational tension rises, producing a paradox in which individual caregivers meet criteria while the system fails; family friction is translated by professional discourse into deficient capacity; and at the points where caregiving arrangements change, intervention continuity and the institutional interface break down at the same time. title: AI Governance in Smart Cities: Religious Freedom and Fundamental Rights
journal: Proceedings of the International Conference on AI Research.
abstract: Artificial intelligence increasingly structures urban mobility, security, welfare, planning and participation. This article asks when AI-enabled smart-city governance may interfere with, or indirectly burden, freedom of religion or belief and which safeguards should govern that risk. It is principally a doctrinal and functional comparative legal study, supported by a bounded documentary examination of Hassan, Bridges, SyRI, the CJEU automated-decision cases and Amsterdam's crowd-monitoring infrastructure. The materials are selected to compare recurring mechanisms of identification, classification, allocation and procedural opacity across different jurisdictions and evidentiary settings. Their role is to provide factual anchoring by documenting systems, allegations as characterised by courts and legal findings; they do not support prevalence estimates or constitute empirical research in the social-scientific sense. The analysis identifies three forms of technologically mediated interference. Direct interference uses religion, belief or a belief-related site as a criterion; indirect interference arises through neutral proxies or optimisation rules that create particular disadvantage; ambient interference results when traceability, inaccessible participation and repeated administrative friction cumulatively chill or obstruct protected conduct. title: Current-driven Magnetic Skyrmions for Encoding/Storing Information: Manipulation and Dynamics in Nanoscale Structures
abstract: This dissertation investigates the dynamics of current-driven magnetic skyrmions, topological solitons in magnetic materials with broken spatial inversion symmetry, for low-power spintronic applications like racetrack memory and multilevel data storage. Skyrmions’ small size and low driving current requirements make them promising information carriers. The research examines skyrmion motion under driving currents, pinning effects, and thermal fluctuations, using numerical simulations (Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert equation), analytical studies (Thiele equation), and theoretical modeling to design novel data storage devices. The study analyzes skyrmion motion amidst pinning potentials from material imperfections. Simulations reveal that thermal fluctuations vary with damping: acting as a frictional force at low damping or a driving force aiding depinning at high damping. The Thiele equation quantifies this, though its accuracy wanes at low temperatures with pinning. The skyrmion Hall angle, influenced by current and pinning, provides insights for ambient-condition devices. These findings underpin a proposed multilevel data storage device, where controlled current positions skyrmions at pinning sites for high-density, low-power encoding. The research also explores altermagnetic (ATM) skyrmions, which exhibit d-wave symmetry via exchange-driven spin splitting. title: Systematic literature review of biochar-modified asphalt: Relationship between biochar type, aging resistance, and carbon emission
abstract: Systematic literature review addressing the alloys-SUS frictional functioning of asphalt with biochar. The review was performed using the PRISMA method with literature obtained from Scopus, Web of Science, ScienceDirect and Google Scholar within the years 2015 to 2026. According to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, a total of 33 eligible studies were included after screening. The results showed that the type of biochar can considerably affect the rheological properties, aging resistance and environmental performance of asphalt. The high aromatic carbon content, porous structure and low volatile matter of biochars derived from lignocellulosic biomass resources such as coconut shell, wood waste, switchgrass and walnut shell lead to much better anti-aging performance. These properties limit asphalt oxidation and prevent carbonyl and sulfoxide group formation during aging. As opposed to low-ash biochars, ash-rich biochars from materials such as rice husk and manure can increase asphalt stiffness but decrease flexibility in low temperatures, offering very limited carbon-emission benefit. This review also indicated that due to its use as a substitute for petroleum-based binders, carbon storage in the pavement system and lower volatile organic compound emissions during asphalt production, biochar reduces net carbon-emission. title: COMPUTATIONAL GEOMETRY AND ORIGAMI-INSPIRED MANIFOLDS IN NEUROENDOVASCULAR DEVICE SCIENCE
journal: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
abstract: Neuroendovascular devices must reconcile a small delivery profile with sufficient working dimensions, flexibility, force transmission and biological compatibility within fragile, tortuous vessels. Origami-inspired engineering offers a mathematical language for prescribing transitions between compact and functional configurations. Its relevance extends beyond miniaturisation to deployment sequencing, local compliance, surface coverage, payload protection and potentially reversible manipulation. This narrative review examines the evidence for folding architectures in stents and catheter-mounted structures, their relationship to cerebral flow-diverter mechanics, and their possible integration with endovascular micro- and nanorobotics. Existing research establishes geometric and manufacturing feasibility, but does not establish a general safety advantage in human cerebral vessels. Particular distinctions are required between structural origami, compliant or kirigami mechanisms, magnetically actuated particle collectives and molecular DNA origami. These platforms share opportunities for programmed transformation but differ in fabrication, actuation, transport, tracking and biological fate. Potential neurointerventional applications include compact retrieval cages, conformable scaffolds, controlled distal catheter components and locally triggered therapeutic carriers. abstract: Resonant piezoelectric composite structures provide high output through structural resonance, but their performance is often sensitive to frequency mismatch, load variation, and changes in contact conditions. This study develops a frequency-tolerant resonant quadruped robot using piezoelectric–carbon-fiber composite beams and a Contact-Modulated Inertial Driving (CMID) mechanism. Each driving leg consists of PZT-5H piezoelectric layers bonded to a carbon-fiber substrate. Under asymmetric sawtooth-wave excitation near the first order bending resonance, the robot exhibits directional locomotion. A proposed contact modulation mechanism relates the structural response to possible changes in foot–ground contact conditions and the distribution of sticking and slipping over each cycle. title: Design and Repeatability Testing of a Novel Benchtop Apparatus for Evaluating Wear Durability of Artificial Tendons
abstract: Artificial tendons are potential alternatives to biological grafts for reconstructing large tendon defects, yet their clinical translation is limited partly by mechanical durability during repetitive gliding against pulley-like structures (e.g., retinacula). Standardized methods for evaluating long-term tendon-pulley wear under physiologically relevant conditions are lacking. This study aimed to develop a benchtop testing methodology for mechanical wear of artificial tendons after high-cycle loading. A custom apparatus was designed to simulate key biomechanical features of the flexor pollicis longus tendon, including tensile load, excursion velocity, and wrapping angle at the tendon-pulley interface. Apparatus performance and repeatability were evaluated using polyester tendons subjected to 1.02 million simulated thumb flexions, equivalent to approximately 395 days of simulated physiological thumb motion, at a rate of 22.1 simulated flexions per second. Non-lubricated testing resulted in excessive frictional heating (93 °C within 40,800 simulated thumb flexions), causing premature thermal damage and ultimate tensile strength (UTS) variability. Conversely, applying boundary lubricant at the tendon-pulley interface, mimicking synovial fluid, maintained temperatures at approximately 36 °C and eliminated non-physiological thermal degradation. title: A study on porosity formation in cold-spray additively manufactured 6061 aluminium parts using MIG, TIG and FSW welding processes
journal: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
abstract: Cold Spray Additive Manufacturing (CSAM) is a solid-state additive manufacturing process that enables components to be produced and repaired without melting the deposited material. However, limited research has examined the weldability of CSAM components. This study investigates porosity formation and local hardness responses in CSAM 6061 aluminium joined using Tungsten Inert Gas (TIG), Metal Inert Gas (MIG), and Friction Stir Welding (FSW), considering both non-heat-treated (NHT) and heat-treated (HT) conditions. Macroscopic, micrographic, ImageJ-based porosity analysis and Vickers hardness measurements were used to characterise the welded regions. TIG and MIG produced substantial fusion zone porosity with characteristics consistent with hydrogen-assisted pore formation during melting and solidification. Pre-weld heat treatment reduced the measured two-dimensional pore area fraction from 26.3% to 18.6% for TIG and from 30.7% to 22.1% for MIG, while also altering pore size and spatial distribution. TIG exhibited relatively large, interconnected pores extending from the fusion boundary, whereas MIG showed a greater population of smaller pores concentrated towards the upper weld region. Both fusion processes produced local hardness reductions, with hardness recovery of approximately 50–56% for TIG and 63–67% for MIG relative to the corresponding control regions. abstract: Introduction. Risarthrosis is one of the common causes of disability in patients. Traditional interventions - trapezectomy and arthrodesis - have a number of serious complications. title: Relying on Personal Means to Make it Through and Hoping for the Best: A Situational Analysis of Teacher Candidates’ Well-being During Field Experiences in Alberta, Canada
journal: ERA: Education and Research Archive (University of Alberta)
abstract: Practical field experiences in teacher education are unique and under-explored settings for health promotion that are situationally bound with the teacher preparation programs and the K-12 school systems they bridge. Practical field experiences that attend to well-being provide an optimal learning environment for teacher candidates and nurture their development within the profession. As important components of instruction and extensions of their campuses, teacher education programs share in the responsibility for thriving practical field experiences, though most lack the resources, mechanisms, and influence to meaningfully promote health and well-being in the K-12 settings where they take place. This study explored how well-being is encountered and negotiated by teacher candidates in Alberta during their practical field experiences and the key elements, materialities, discourses, structures, and conditions that characterize the situation. Situational analysis was used to develop a detailed portrait of the elements and their relations, the collective actors and meso-level interpretations, and discursive positions present in the situation. Eight participants holding various roles in field experience were interviewed virtually and 23 documents were reviewed to generate data that was analyzed through the development of situational, social worlds/arenas, and positional maps. title: Pore-scale heat transfer in structured packed bed with application in high-grade thermal energy storage
abstract: In this study, the thermofluid performance of structured packed beds for high-temperature thermal energy storage applications is explored. Simple cubic (SC), body-centered cubic (BCC), and face-centered cubic (FCC) particle arrangements are investigated through pore-scale simulations accounting for conduction, surface radiation, fluid flow, and interstitial heat transfer. Based on the pore-scale simulations, correlations are developed for friction factor ( f k ), radiation-free effective conductivity ( k c ), radiative exchange factor ( F ), and volumetric interstitial heat transfer coefficient ( h v ), allowing the radiative conductivity ( k r ) and overall effective thermal conductivity ( k eff ) to be calculated. The pore-scale results and proposed correlations are further assessed through comparisons with experimental data and established empirical and numerical correlations available in the literature. These correlations are coupled with a one-dimensional two-phase (1D-2P) model to assess the performance of a packed bed of 1.5 m length and 1.0 m diameter, subjected to a daily cycle of 3 h charging, 18 h storage, 1 h discharging, and 2 h idle. title: Development and Multi-Objective Optimization of a WER–SBR Composite Modified Emulsified Asphalt for Airport Pavement Preventive Maintenance
abstract: Emulsified asphalt-based fog seals are widely used for the preventive maintenance of airport asphalt pavements. Compared with highway pavements, airport runways and taxiways operate under far more demanding conditions: wide-body aircraft exert tire pressures of 1.2–1.6 MPa while undergoing extreme acceleration during takeoff and severe deceleration during landing, generating coupled vertical compression and horizontal shear forces that conventional single-modifier emulsified asphalts cannot reliably withstand. Surface degradation at airports also carries direct flight-safety consequences—raveled aggregate becomes foreign object debris (FOD), and loss of surface texture compromises braking friction—making high-performance preventive maintenance materials far more critical for airports than for highways. This study develops a waterborne epoxy resin (WER)–styrene-butadiene rubber (SBR) composite modified emulsified asphalt integrating high toughness, ultraviolet (UV) aging resistance, and Wettability to meet these stringent airport requirements. Fluorescence microscopy reveals that the polymer undergoes dense polymerization and continuous changes, which may construct an interpenetrating polymer network (IPN); the optimal WER content for network integrity is 15%. An L16(44) orthogonal experiment is designed with WER content, solid content, UV absorber content, and hydrophobic agent content as factors and bond strength, viscosity aging index, and contact angle as responses. The data comprise three complementary components.
